text:
maria: FYI we got a noisy alert from backup-bot about restores failing for a handful of archived DB snapshots. looks like metadata is missing (no CMK id) so KMS grants aren't applied on restore :grimacing:
backup-bot: ALERT 1735802480 - 6 restores failed in the last 30m. sample errors: "decrypt failed: missing key metadata". s3/gcs objects uploaded by backup-agent v2.1.0
aj: pinging encops. do we know if this is an uploader config change or a KMS propagation issue? :thinking:
samir: quick summary: last deploy in canary replaced multipart uploader lib with a fork to fix throughput. that fork accidentally drops custom object headers starting with "x-encrypt-" when composing multipart parts. looks like our CMK id was stored in x-encrypt-cmk header. :facepalm:
maria: ok that matches the timeline. which backups are affected? customer-facing or internal only?
leo: quick check against the retention archive shows ~420 objects from 2026-03-19 00:00 to 2026-03-21 08:00 with missing x-encrypt-cmk. probable window = deploy window. only some tenants (multi-part > 5GB).
aj: can you paste the command you used to confirm?
leo: here's the gsutil metadata check I ran:
```
gsutil stat gs://redwood-backups-prod/tenant-12345/db-snap-20260320.tar.gz
# output snippet
Content-Type: application/octet-stream
x-goog-meta-backup-id: db-snap-20260320
x-goog-meta-opaque: true
# x-encrypt-cmk: MISSING
```

leo: also ran `aws s3api head-object` for S3 uploads, same absence of `x-amz-meta-x-encrypt-cmk` header.
nancy: are audit logs showing KMS grant requests for these restores? we need to know whether restores attempted to use a grant and were rejected, or never attempted because metadata absent.
samir: checked CloudAudit + KMS logs: no decrypt attempts for these object IDs. restore workflow aborts early when metadata isn't present, so we don't generate KMS Audit entries. that explains silence.
maria: immediate mitigation — can we fall back to tenant-default CMK from tenant manifest when header missing? what are the risks?
aj: fallback is possible but risky: tenant-default CMK isn't necessarily allowed for historical snapshots (customers can opt different keys). also could violate key-scoping/escrow policies. we need sign-off from security.
nancy: we should not auto-fallback until we confirm owner intent. short-term we can enable a controlled-path manual restore that allows ops to specify a CMK via CLI after verifying tenant request.
leo: engineering quick fix: revert multipart uploader fork to upstream v2.0.7 which preserves metadata. I can roll that to canary in 15m and to prod in the next deploy window if tests pass.
maria: sounds good. who owns the rollout?
leo: assigning to me. I'll open a PR and link the revert. expected ETA: canary in 1h, prod in 6h after smoke tests.
samir: we also need a migration/repair plan for affected objects: two options — recompose/reupload from source archives (preserves headers) or attach CMK metadata via a metadata-edit operation (GCS supports compose + metadata replace for some objects). reupload is safer for integrity.
aj: cost/effort for reupload? how many objects and size?
leo: ~420 objects, avg 12GB = ~5TB total. reupload bandwidth + egress cost but doable over 24-48h using parallel workers and bucket-to-bucket copy that preserves kms if we set metadata on write. will coordinate with infra for bandwidth throttles.
maria: create a ticket with the migration plan and customer impact matrix. Samir, Nancy — please draft the communication template for ops to follow when contacting affected tenants. include verification checklist.
samir: will do. recommend we include proof-of-possession steps (recent activity, billing contact) before performing manual restore.
nancy: also add audit requirement: any manual restore must have an entry in the encryptops audit channel and include the operator's ephemeral grant id. we need that for post-mortem and compliance.
eng-oncall-bot: note created: #INC-2026-249 - backup-agent metadata-strip v2 uploader. assigned to leo. severity P2.
leo: linking PR: https://github.com/redwood/backup-agent/pull/1287 (revert uploader fork). will kick tests now.
maria: good. timeline summary: 1) revert in canary (leo) - 1h 2) smoke tests (qa) - 3h 3) prod rollout (leo) - 6h 4) migration plan ticket (leo) - draft in 2h 5) ops manual restore path + comms (samir/nancy) - draft in 2h
aj: forensics: we should snapshot all current objects and log which ones lack CMK metadata before any repair so we can prove original state. leo can you produce an export list?
leo: yes I'll produce a CSV with object id, tenant, size, upload timestamp, missing-header-flag. pushing to s3://redwood-incident-artifacts/INC-2026-249/manifest.csv
maria: thanks. after prod revert, plan to run a small pilot reupload for 2 tenants and verify restore end-to-end with KMS audit entries. no auto-repair until pilot succeeds. :white_check_mark:
samir: note on long-term: add test in CI that composes multipart uploads in a way that verifies customer metadata are preserved. and add a gating check in deploy pipeline for any uploader lib change.
leo: agreed. adding tests now. PR description will include rollout gates.
nancy: also update the runbook: "restore when CMK header missing" with legal hold and key-ownership checks.
maria: thanks everyone. any objections to priority/approach?
aj: none. :thumbsup:
leo: starting canary now. will update thread with canary deploy ts and smoke results.
maria: keep posting short status updates here. we'll convert to a postmortem if customer impact > 1 tenant or any compliance alerts.
eng-oncall-bot: canary deployed 1735804868 to canary cluster-3. automated smoke passed for basic upload/download checks.
leo: smoke uncovered one edge-case where object compose in GCS returned 412 on metadata replace. filing follow-up to fallback to reupload for that object.
samir: ok, I'm starting customer comm drafts. will share in #encryptops-comms and cc legal infra.
maria: great. closing loop later today. :lock:
